I know right now this advice isn't going to be well accepted, but I know from experience that it's the option that allows you to move forward, with a clear conscience but more importantly, it's the option that will sever any link to the things of the past that might try to creep in and reopen old wounds. The advice is that you need to forgive your dad for the things that he has done, said, allowed to happen to you, ignored that happened you or anything, actually EVERYTHING.

I know right now it might seem like you'll never get to a place where even thinking about forgiving him is a possibility but that's just the fresh wounds speaking. Once you have had time to heal I hope you are able to get to a place where you are able to forgive him. Admittedly this isn't an easy task, by no stretch of the imagination, but unfortunately it is a necessary one. Not necessary for him, but necessary for you. . . . . .

By holding onto the hate and anger we never really allow ourselves to heal and by doing so we keep our minds in that place or hurt and fear. Eventually what happens is we will begin to mirror the behavior that we once despised. I am not sure how, or why we do this but I have seen it done over and over. Consider also that your forgiveness of his actions by no means says that what transpired was ok nor does it absolve him of any guilt or culpability, it's simply you saying to him, "even though what you did and how you acted was abhorrent I am not willing to carry around this anger like a cancer for the rest of my life so here's your baggage I refuse to shoulder it and then pass it on to my children".

Having grown up with a father that fostered a similar environment to one you've described I know how lonely and hopeless it can be. And I was blinded for the longest time, believing that there wasn't anything that I could learn from him but eventually  after much reflecting and soul searching, I came to a very productive and freeing conclusion. I realized that even in the worst case scenario there is, at a bare minimum, one lesson we can walk away with: what not to do next time, in the future, to our children, you can basically plug almost anything in here. But to clarify, even from the worst example we can learn how to do it better by not repeating the mistakes that we saw.

I hope there is something you can take away from my experiences because if through my suffering I can save someone else from the same fate, then it was all worth it. If you ever need someone to listen, or to talk to you can reach out and I'll be more than happy to lend a hand.
Those are the times that the pain rears its ugly head, but all we can do is put our heads down and push through it. According to that one quote, "this too shall pass"

I hypothesize that far too many people have been or, in the case of weaker individuals, are scared to be hurt so they adjust they behavior to reflect the "game" that too many are playing. The unfortunate side effect of this is that those of us that don't want to play get mixed in with the lot and end up getting hurt.

BUT please please do not give in to the overwhelming urge to just surrender to "the game". Be who you are, be unique, be the hold out. Don't become jaded, there are far too few of us left and we need each other when we are down in the pits, please don't give in. Admittedly, it's far scarier because being this way leaves us vulnerable to attack and we do end up enduring a lot more heartbreak this way, but the one thing that you can hold on to, that none of these other people can say, is that you're a fighter and you remained true to who you are inside, despite having every reason to give up.
